context.requirement_text: REQ-459 (docs/requirements.yaml ~34475, owner CODE-DESIGNER, stage S3, depends_on REQ-447, REQ-455): design-only entry. Writes a design artefact in lib/letflow/design/, no application code, for two refusals added to Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task: rule A (distinct person, distinct_from) and rule C (required decision outputs, required_outputs). Binding constraints Rule A: identity is the user id never the role (also for an API token); enforced at completion (authority) and claim (early feedback); no role exempt, TENANT_ADMIN included; compare against the MOST RECENT completion of each named node in the same instance; attribute optional and off by default; refusal is a clean 4xx with zero detail beyond 'separation of duties'; REQ-455 validator WARNS (REQ-464) on distinct_from naming a node routed to the same single-member role (design specifies inputs only); PROCESS-AUDITOR B1 follow-up recorded in REQ-463 open_questions. Rule C: check runs on the server before any state change; form 'required' stays a UI hint (REQ-273); validator also flags a decision reading a key no upstream task declares in required_outputs; out-of-enum value is a retryable 422, no instance ERROR, refusal before anything is written, task stays open and claimable. Twelve numbered sections required (1 schema+codes, 2 one check order, 3 422 body, 4 rule A body/status, 5 audit record, 6 claim path, 7 API-token identity, 8 rework semantics, 9 D-ESC, 10 idempotency/replay, 11 other merge paths + REQ-061/0007 amendment, 12 test plan). BA decisions 2026-10-07: assign/reassign do not check distinct_from; parallel branches compare against completions existing at check time; a never-completed named node imposes no constraint; FormExpressionReevaluation errors stay EXECUTION_ERROR.

task.description: WF-02 step 03 (RELEASE-VALIDATOR): independent re-verification of REQ-459's five acceptance criteria against the design file itself and the code on the branch. Design-only requirement: no application code to run; mix test, scripts/test_parallel.sh and mix letflow.check.test were NOT run (design-only diff, and the dispatcher ruled out suite runs because of RAM; nothing under lib/ other than the design markdown, nothing under test/, changed).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a design file under lib/letflow/design/ exists with the twelve numbered sections, each answering its question and naming file and function; no implementation code beyond @spec-level signatures and a numbered check order

AC2: section 2 gives one total order of every check and write in run_complete_task for both rules and states, per refusal path, that nothing is written before the refusal except the one audit record; re-derived from lib/letflow/engine.ex independently
AC3: each binding constraint of rule A and rule C appears as a traceability row; none weakened or re-decided
AC4: sections 3 and 4 give literal example response bodies; the rule A body contains only 'separation of duties' and a status
AC5: checked by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and every cited file path and function exists on the branch, verified by grep and quoted

result.summary: All five acceptance criteria hold on independent re-verification. Formed my own view from the design file and lib/letflow/engine.ex before reading any earlier handoff. Branch diff vs origin/main is the design file plus handoff JSONs only; docs/requirements.yaml and decision record 0007 are untouched. No blocking finding; four non-blocking observations.

The design's 2.2 order is identical, with the NEW :completion_guards step correctly placed between :snapshot_and_state (2277) and :form_expression_reevaluation (2280), i.e. after both row locks.

merge_output_variables/7 (3875-3903): VariableSchema.variable_validations/5 then apply_variable_merge/6 (3916-3943), whose {:rejected,...} clause (3928-3941) builds the ERROR args; matches design 6b-i..6b-v, including the 'unreachable, retained as guard' disposition.

Tail write order re-derived from build_complete_task_tail_multi (4328-4506): first clause (4328-4341) ExecutionError.append_multi; second clause: build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi (4383; inside it {:hop_chain_token_records} 4637, task records via maybe_append_task_activation_multi -> TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records, then reconcile_token_records -> :token_reconciliation 4838), timer arms 4413, service-task dispatch 4436, :task_complete 4448, :cancel_escalation_timers 4458, audit 4470, :event 4473, :projection 4482, sub-process children 4491, completion cascade 4498, :complete_task_outcome 4505 = design W1..W13 in the same order. Step 7 region (4020-4330) contains no repo/Repo insert/update/delete and no Multi.insert/update (awk scan: 0 hits), so 'no writes before the tail' holds.

Refusal path handling verified: a Multi.run returning {:error,_} yields {:error, step, reason, changes}, which skips every tail step; maybe_snapshot_after_complete_task has clauses only for {:ok,...} (2418, 2434) plus the pass-through at 2454, and emit_task_completed_telemetry only for {:ok,...} (2384) plus pass-through 2405, so neither writes or emits on a refusal. interpret_complete_result catch-all (5307) has changes.task available (step 1 ran). The design's 2.3 table states for REFUSE-A, REFUSE-C1 and REFUSE-C2 'NOTHING' written before the refusal, only locks and SELECTs, exactly one audit record written afterwards by a separate transaction (2.4, modelled on record_task_activation_rejection_audit at engine.ex:4979, the ISS-0784 precedent), and states the at-most-one-record guarantee honestly (D-3).
Step 8z (rescue -> {:transaction_failed, exception}, 500, no refusal audit) is stated, which matches engine.ex:2362-2364. Locks: only the two existing; no new lock. Precedence list (2.5) is coherent.

Traceability table (lines 923-944) has rows A1-A11 and C1-C7. Compared against the requirement description bullets: Rule A bullets = user id (A1), completion+claim (A2), no role exempt (A3), most recent completion (A4), optional/off (A5), clean 4xx with zero detail (A6), REQ-455 warning inputs (A7), PROCESS-AUDITOR B1 follow-up (A8), plus the three BA rulings (A9 assign/reassign, A10 parallel, A11 never-completed). Rule C bullets = server before any state change (C1), form 'required' stays a hint (C2), validator flags undeclared decision key (C3), 422 and no ERROR (C4), plus BA rulings null=missing/empty string by schema (C5), reevaluation unchanged (C6), and REQ-460's submitted-only (C7). Every bullet has a row; none re-decided.

Scoped relaxations found (all stated in the design, none silent): (1) C4 / REQ-460 'naming the rejected key(s)': rejected-key names are restricted to the task's own form_schema.properties plus required_outputs; an out-of-form rejection still refuses but names nothing (section 3.2, Adjustments REQ-460 item 0, SECURITY-REVIEWER F-1). The refusal and no-state-change are not weakened; only name disclosure is narrowed. The C4 traceability row itself does not mention this narrowing (see finding F-1). (2) C3: the warning fires only when some upstream HUMAN_TASK form produces the key and none declares it (section 1.4), and is a permanent WARNING, not a violation (D-4). The binding text says 'flags', so this reads literally; it is flagged as D-4 and OQ-3, and requires an ORCH reword of REQ-462 acceptance line 4 (Adjustments REQ-462 item 0/2). (3) A5/C1 default-off: the design states the schema-rejection 422 applies on every HUMAN_TASK completion, including nodes with neither attribute (2.2 step 4a), which is the binding C4 text ('any value a variable_schema rejects on this path'). Not weakened.
Also flagged and consistent with the binding text: the rule A body is a constant two-member document (D-1); claim refusal uses 403 rather than the router's 409 for eligibility refusals (D-2).
Section 3.2 gives two literal application/problem+json 422 bodies (missing_keys ["decision"], and rejected_keys ["decision"]), no submitted value, no enum, no ids.

Section 4.2 gives the literal rule A body, exactly: {"detail":"separation of duties","status":403}. Only the phrase and a status; no type, title, trace_id, ids, or node names. The design states why the standard five-member envelope is not used (trace_id would break byte-identity).
